We require, phenol, conc. Sulphuric acid (or liquid paraffin), capillary tube, thermometer, thread, iron stand with clamp,test tube, beaker, stirrer, wire gauze, tripod stand, Bunsen burner etc.
Take the test tube.
Using a dropper take a small quantity of phenol.
Fill up to two-third of the test tube with phenol.
Fix the test tube to the thermometer with the thread.The thread should be fixed near the mouth of the test tube.
Take conc. sulphuric acid.
Fill the beaker with conc. sulphuric acid using a funnel.
Place the beaker on the wire gauze placed over the Bunsen burner and insert a stirrer in it.
Clamp the thermometer carrying the test tube in the iron stand. Lower the thermometer along with the test tube into conc. sulphuric acid bath.
Adjust the thermometer so that its bulb is well under the acid and open end of the tube with the thread is sufficiently outside the acid bath.
Take a capillary tube 5-6 cm in length and seal one end of the tube by heating it in the flame and giving a slight twist.
Place the capillary in the test tube with closed end upward.
Heat the the sulphuric acid bath slowly and stir the liquid with the stirrer by moving it up and down.
After some time bubbles will start coming from the end of the capillary tube dipping in the liquid, but soon a rapid and continupus stream of air bubbles escapes from it.
This is the stage when vapour pressure of the liquid in th sealed capillary just exceeds the atmospheric pressure.
Note the temperature (t1)when continuous stream of air bubbles starts coming out.
Turn off the burner.
Bubbles from the end of te capillary tube goes on decreasing.
Note the temperature (t2) when evolution of bubbles from the end of the capillary just stops.
Calculate the boiling point of phenol using the formula ,( t1 ° + t2 °)/2
